Point query

Click the map for Site Intel: left rail shows every signal (including DNREC septic); right deck opens full detail — septic shows soil-boring attributes and site-eval records with DEN links. Infil from AASHTO / HYDGRP / septic. Lateral radius default 500 ft; column 0–50 ft.

Project limits

Draw a polygon around the project. Analyze inventories everything inside, marks the best screening infiltration cell, and writes a qualitative site summary (soils, hydro, constraints, brownfield / UST / landfill flags). Screening only — not App.1 or Phase I ESA.
Click Draw, then click map vertices. Double-click or Close to finish (≥3 points).

Search radius 500 ft

Loaded layers

Open project folder to load refs/.

Phase 2 hydro grids

FirstMap DGS dry/normal/wet grids (Coastal Plain) + Sussex unconfined aquifer T/thickness/base. Blender weights DTW with Open-Meteo precip vs 10-yr normals + season — screening only. Piedmont DTW is usually NoData. Needs internet. Run download-all-refs.bat for the full polygon/point pack.
No query yet.

Reference layers

Drop FirstMap / DNREC GeoJSON here, or run download-all-refs.bat into refs/ then Open project folder. Pack includes geology, soils, WRPA, wetlands, flood, tax ditches, DNREC septic, coastal, roads, plus nrcs_de_by_mukey.json, infil_anchors.json (from import-infil-pdfs.bat), and dgir_wells.json (from download-dgir-wells.bat — DGS lith / geophys log inventory). Paged files with the same base name merge. Empty files are skipped.
Drop GeoJSON / infil_anchors.json / dgir_wells.json here (or click)
Field infil anchors: drop DelDOT M&R Borehole Infiltration Test PDFs into infil-pdfs\, run import-infil-pdfs.bat, then reload refs. Map shows amber diamonds; Site Intel → Anchors lists measured rates (design = ÷2.5 for 4″ borehole).
DGS DGIR wells: run download-dgir-wells.bat → refs/dgir_wells.json. Teal markers = lithologic / geophysical log sites (PDF/LAS links). Site Intel → DGS. Classic DGIR GeoServer interval text is not bundled when maps.dgs.udel.edu is offline.

Boring database

Borings come from db.json. Export feature store joins each mapped boring to geology / soils (HYDGRP) / recharge / lab stats, a screening infiltration band, and a DNREC borehole FoS 2.5 design-rate band (est ÷ 2.5). Then run build-mukey-priors.bat to write refs/mukey_priors.json (statewide analogs). Map clicks show the same. Screening ≠ field-verified ASTM rate.

Generate geo-report draft

Signal poles (optional) — boring · location · type · length

Site layer preview

Select a job with mapped borings to preview Sections 2 & 4 from loaded reference layers.
Yellow-highlighted fields need engineer input. Section 8 stays with the PE — the Computed Observations annex holds strata, N, and pole cases. Section 3.2 is filled from FirstMap depth-to-water grids (and optional climate-blended current estimate) when online sampling is on; Section 3.1 (HA atlas) still needs engineer citation. The DNREC draft follows BMP Appendix 1 §IV structure — screening rates with FoS 2.5 are labeled; field ASTM tests / PE seal still required for submittal.

notes

Pipeline: pick a site (or import a new job) → the generator assembles a .docx draft in the DelDOT memo format with computed content: header block · Section 2 Area Geology from the surficial geology polygon at the site · Section 3 water table (DGIR grids + HA atlas citation) · Section 4 recharge class (Kent & Sussex) · Sections 5–7 from parsed logs and lab data (ground cover, groundwater readings, moisture ranges, strata, N-value profiles) · appendices (summary table, N-vs-depth charts, boring plan). Section 8 Recommendations stays with the engineer.
DelDOT GeoTrak
Geotechnical site intelligence

Informational use only

DelDOT GeoTrak compiles historic boring records and public reference mapping to support site reconnaissance and draft documentation.

This tool does not replace project-specific subsurface exploration, laboratory testing, engineering judgment, or applicable DelDOT design standards and requirements.

Outputs (including map queries and draft .docx reports) are for informational and supplemental use. A licensed professional engineer remains responsible for interpretation, recommendations, and sealed documents.
